beats.say: Is this username already taken? Checking billions of names in a database is slow and expensive.

beats.text: A tiny bit array: definitely not, or maybe.
beats.say: A Bloom filter is a tiny array of bits that answers one question: definitely not here, or maybe here.

beats.text: Add: hash it, set those bits to 1.
beats.say: To add an item, run it through several hash functions. Each one picks a position, and we set those bits to one.

beats.text: Any bit is 0? Definitely not in the set.
beats.say: To check an item, hash it the same way. If any bit is zero, the item is definitely not in the set.

beats.text: All bits 1? Maybe. It can be a false positive.
beats.say: If all the bits are one, the item is probably there. But it could be a false positive, because other items may have set those bits.
So a Bloom filter never has false negatives, only false positives, and it uses a tiny fraction of the memory. Perfect for skipping expensive lookups.
